title: Tool Use and Agents on the API

questions.prompt: Order one round of the tool-use loop.

items.text: Your code sends back a tool_result matched by tool_use_id
You send a request with tool definitions
Claude continues: more tool calls or a final answer
Claude responds with stop_reason tool_use and tool_use blocks
Your code runs the requested tool

questions.explanation: Define tools, Claude requests a call, you execute it, return the result, and Claude continues until it finishes.

questions.prompt: Claude makes three tool calls in one response. How should you return the results?

options.text: All three tool_result blocks together in a single user message
As plain text in the system prompt

questions.explanation: Return all parallel results in one user message. Splitting them across messages discourages Claude from making parallel calls.

questions.prompt: When a tool fails, return a tool_result with "____": true and a helpful message instead of dropping it.
questions.explanation: Reporting errors as is_error results lets Claude recover, for example by fixing the input or explaining the problem.

questions.prompt: Match each approach to who runs the loop and the infrastructure.

pairs.right: The SDK runs the loop; you host
Claude Code's harness and built-in tools as a library; you host
Anthropic runs the loop and hosts a sandbox per session

questions.explanation: Only Managed Agents supplies both the harness and the hosted deployment; the others leave hosting to you.

questions.prompt: Which criteria should all hold before you build an agent? Select all that apply.

options.text: The task is multi-step and hard to specify in advance
The outcome justifies higher cost and latency
Errors can be caught and recovered from
Agents are always better than simple workflows

questions.explanation: Complexity, value, viability, and recoverable errors should all hold. Otherwise a single call or a coded workflow is simpler and more reliable.

questions.prompt: Code that forces tool_choice to a specific tool now fails on Claude Opus 5.5. What should you do instead?

options.text: Use auto with a prompt instruction and strict: true, or structured outputs if you only wanted JSON
Retry the same request until it works
Prefill the assistant turn with the tool name

questions.explanation: Forced tool choice returns a 400 on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Fable 5.1. Use auto plus instructions and strict schemas, or structured outputs.
